posts.title: Four rounds, one code: how a monitoring year is kept
posts.excerpt: Seisui Environmental runs 38 sites at four rounds a year, and the named places on the River Wend show what that ledger is for.
posts.content:
Seisui Environmental has kept a monitoring ledger since the practice opened in 2009. The count we publish is 38 sites, 16 years, and 4 rounds a year. An annual programme for one site costs $6,600 and buys those four visits. A round is not a fresh opinion under a new title. It is a return to a coded place, sampled in the way already agreed, so a council or a landowner can read this season beside an earlier one. The office that holds the file is at 14 Millrace Lane, Alder Bridge, on the River Wend, and it is open Mon–Fri 08:30–17:30.

The earliest river start we name is on the Wend itself. WR-01 is the Wend River at Mill Weir, surface water, on the ledger since 2012. WR-04 is the Wend River at Ferry Steps, kept since 2015 with those river sites. PD-05 is the mill pond at Alder Bridge, surface water, since 2018. A single bottle at a bank can be useful, and we still sell that visit on its own: a water quality sampling round, up to 6 points, at $2,250, with laboratory results due in 15 working days. The reason for a programme is the next quarter, and the quarter after that, under one instruction. Laboratory courier beyond 60 km, and tax, sit outside either fee.

Groundwater uses the same habit and a different medium. GW-07 is the Hollin village wells. In 2024 the parish council there instructed a groundwater quality programme for 5 wells. Five points sit inside the six-point limit of a water round, so the five wells are one site on the annual fee, not five separate programmes. GW-09 is the Copse Farm borehole, on the ledger since 2019, also groundwater. Both keep their codes. The report lists what was sampled and what the laboratory returned. It does not describe either place as safe to drink, and it does not carry a pass mark. Dr Ilse Varga leads the hydrology. She founded the practice in 2009, and the rule she still uses is to name the site before interpreting it.

Soil and habitat stay on the same table so nobody has to pretend that a meadow and a former industrial lot are one kind of question. SL-02 is the former tannery lot at Fennick Road, soil, since 2023. A private landowner commissioned Phase I and Phase II there before resale. Phase I is $3,400. Phase II is from $8,900, agreed before the ground is opened. SL-06 is Station yard, kept with the soil codes since 2022. WM-03 is Wend Meadow, habitat, since 2021, where Alder Bridge council asked for a floodplain meadow restoration baseline and 3-year monitoring. Habitat fieldwork runs from April to September, and the survey fee is $4,200. A baseline records the vegetation that was there. Tomas Brandt leads soil and contamination. Amara Okonkwo leads the ecology. The sentence we will stand behind is that the instructed work was done and reported.

The jobs around a round are deliberately narrow. Lucía Ferreira leads field sampling: the points, the bottles, and the cool box back to Millrace Lane. Noah Bakker handles laboratory quality assurance and releases a result only when it matches the scope, inside the 15 working days. Henrik Aalto keeps the GIS and the ledger, and a code is opened only when an instruction starts. Priya Raman handles permitting and municipal liaison when the client is a council or a parish. She uses the same USD fees, with 50% due on instruction and 50% due on the report, and she does not speak as the authority. Those four, with Dr Ilse Varga, Tomas Brandt and Amara Okonkwo, are the seven people on the published list. The address is also the sample store.

A new site still enters in a fixed order. The scoping call is free, lasts 20 minutes, and is held within 2 working days. You can book it on +1 555 0142 300 or at hello@seisui-environmental.example. Desk study and walkover follow within 10 working days, and that step is $1,850 when it is instructed alone. Sampling and the laboratory come next where the scope calls for them. A written report and a 45-minute review meeting close the work. Field days are by arrangement, and weekends and public holidays are closed. Bring a place and the decision in front of you. We can tell you what the water, the soil or the habitat showed on the visits you instructed. The land's future behaviour is not a line in the fee list, and it is not a line we add to the report.

Read across a year, the ledger is a quiet object. Four dates, one code, one medium, and a report each time: that is the whole promise of the $6,600 programme. Mill Weir has been in that pattern since 2012. Hollin's five wells only entered in 2024, so their file is short, and a short file is still an honest one. Station yard, Copse Farm, Ferry Steps, the mill pond and Wend Meadow sit between those dates, each with its own start and its own reason for being instructed. If your place is not among the eight we name, it can still be one of the 38 once you instruct it. Until that day it does not have a code, and we do not write as if it did.
